newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala and Belize to discuss border conflict.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala and Belize to discuss border conflict.

text.p: Guatemala and Belize will hold talks before the weekend in Miami to discuss for the first time in six years their 150-year-old territory dispute, a diplomatic source said on Thursday.
"The two sides are due to meet for preliminary talks. The main focus is believed to be an exchange of views as to respective interpretations of previous bilateral agreements," the source said.
If there is no way to negotiate a bilateral settlement, Guatemala wants both sides to seek outside arbitration, perhaps by the International Court of Justice in The Hague.
Guatemala, which for years claimed Belize as its own, granted its tiny neighbour diplomatic recognition in 1991, while still maintaining some territorial claims over its territory.
In 1994 the Guatemalan government formed a Council on Belize to establish its legal position in the border dispute, but negotiations left off in 1991 were never renewed.

According to Guatemala's foreign affairs minister, Guatemala's negotiators in the mission this week were Luis Alberto Padilla, a special foreign affairs advisor and Antonio Castellanos, the Guatemalan ambassador in Belize.
Miguel Angel Mena, Belize's ambassador in Guatemala was to be part of the Belize mission.
The source said Guatemala's would stick to its traditional demand that Belize cede territory. Historically, Belize has said it will not give up an inch.

Guatemala in the past has demanded retribution from Great Britain as part of a settlement. Britain recently reiterated an offer of a $22 million grant as part of a settlement of the territorial dispute.
Belize, bordered by Mexico and Guatemala, and formerly known as British Honduras, was a British colony until 1981. Britain withdrew its 45-year-old military presence in 1994.
Guatemala's claim to Belize originates in a 1859 border treaty signed with Britain. Guatemala says Britain broke its agreement to build a road between the two countries.
